title: Vero Beach Museum of Art hosts first U.S. stop for Hokusai, Hiroshige, Hasui: Japanese Landscapes in Print
summary: Discover globally celebrated Japanese artworks when the internationally touring Hokusai, Hiroshige, Hasui: Japanese Landscapes in Print, makes its first U.S. stop at the Vero Beach Museum of Art (VBMA) from November 21, 2026, through February 7, 2027. This magnificent exhibition of more than 100 works was organized by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, which holds the finest and largest collection of Japanese art outside of Japan. Hokusai, Hiroshige, Hasui: Japanese Landscapes in Print is VBMA’s first presentation dedicated exclusively to Japanese prints in its 40-year history. It traces more than a century of Japanese landscape printmaking, providing a tour of Japan’s most evocative places, both real and imaginary, while documenting the art and culture of a country that had experienced a profound political, social, cultural, urban, and artistic transformation following the 1868 Meiji Restoration, when Japan dismantled its c

title: Chrysler Museum of Art explores Black identity in "Define Yourself!"
summary: Black representation and identity anchor “Define Yourself!,” an exhibition curated in collaboration with students from Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). On view Nov. 6, 2026-April 25, 2027, at the Chrysler Museum of Art , “Define Yourself!” draws inspiration from James Baldwin’s book, “The Fire Next Time” (1963), in which Baldwin warns the Black community that those who do not define themselves risk being defined by others. The exhibition grapples with themes of self-identification and external perceptions, encouraging viewers to reflect on the ways Black identity is shaped and understood. title: Baseball immortal Babe Ruth knocked it out of the park at Morphy's $2M Toys, Sports & General Collectibles Auction
summary: Three items pertaining to New York Yankees legend Babe Ruth – two vintage baseball cards and a baseball bat signed by the incomparable Sultan of Swat – teamed up to bring in $136,500 at Morphy Auctions’ Toys, Sports & General Collectibles Auction held November 10-12. Loaded with rare, highly desirable antique and vintage items from a wide array of collecting categories, the sale topped $2 million. Many of the headline items will no doubt make wonderful holiday gifts or prized additions to bidders’ collections. The auction’s overall top lot was a 1932 US Caramel Babe Ruth #32 card, graded PSA VG-EX+ 4.5. From a set representing several baseball players, the Ruth card had a deep red background and was centered 70/30 both ways. title: The Problem of the African "Master": A Case for Provable Attribution
summary: When does stylistic similarity become historical fact? The recognition of individual African artists was an important correction to the old assumption that African sculpture was simply the anonymous product of a “tribal style.” But recognizing artistic individuality is not the same as proving that a group of sculptures was carved by one historical individual. Scholars have identified numerous anonymous “master carvers,” including the Master of Buli, Master of Warua, and Master of the Cascade Coiffure. These attributions generally begin with formal comparisons of eyes, mouths, hands, coiffures, proportions, and carving techniques. Sculptures sharing distinctive characteristics are grouped into a presumed individual oeuvre. The problem is that stylistic similarity alone cannot establish common authorship. title: The Henry's iconic James Turrell Skyspace, Light Reign, returns with renewed brilliance
summary: The Henry Art Gallery at the University of Washington celebrates the return of Light Reign, an iconic Skyspace by internationally celebrated artist James Turrell. Following an extensive restoration and a complete transformation of its lighting system, the beloved artwork is once again illuminating the University of Washington campus and inviting visitors to experience light, color, and sky in extraordinary ways. “For more than two decades, Light Reign has been a treasured work in our permanent collection and a landmark in Seattle’s cultural landscape,” says Kris Lewis, John S. title: Geometric abstraction pioneer Leon Polk Smith returns to Los Angeles in two-gallery presentation
summary: Marc Selwyn Fine Art and Lisson Los Angeles present concurrent exhibitions of works by Leon Polk Smith (1906–1996), marking the artist’s first solo exhibition in Los Angeles in more than a decade. Spanning both galleries, the presentations bring together more than twenty paintings alongside a selection of related works on paper, tracing the development and breadth of Smith’s mature practice from the mid-1950s through 1980. Featuring several works never before exhibited, the exhibitions explore Smith’s pioneering investigations of positive and negative space, line, color, and form, revealing the remarkable range of an artist whose approach to geometric abstraction remained both rigorous and inventive. title: Dorotheum's Contemporary Art auction achieves strong results
summary: Following the spectacular opening of the Modern Art auction on 17 November 2026, which made headlines with two world records – for Max Oppenheimer’s “Hess Quartet, String Quartet I” and Alfons Walde’s “Ascent of the Skiers” – Contemporary Art took centre stage on 18 November 2026. International works by artists including Mikuláš Medek, Neo Rauch, Daniel Richter, Yves Klein and Victor Vasarely achieved impressive results. A new world record was also set for a work by Herbert Brandl. The top lot of the auction was Mikuláš Medek’s “Střelnice I – Shooting Range I” from 1971. Bidding for the Czech artist’s Surrealist-inspired painting climbed to €572,000 (estimate €140,000–180,000). title: Christie's New York presents Magnificent Jewels featuring pieces formerly owned by Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis
summary: Christie's presents Magnificent Jewels, a live auction taking place on 8 December at Rockefeller Center in New York City. Bringing together exceptional jewels from distinguished private collections, the sale celebrates extraordinary craftsmanship, rare gemstones, and remarkable provenance. Highlights include jewels formerly owned by Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, alongside important designs by Van Cleef & Arpels, Cartier, Harry Winston, Tiffany & Co., and JAR. Spanning historic treasures and iconic twentieth-century designs, the auction offers a compelling selection of jewels recognized for their artistry, rarity, and the stories behind them. Leading the sale is Magnificent Jewels from the Collection of Mrs. Tom May, a collection of 26 jewels featuring important creations by Van Cleef & Arpels and Harry Winston. title: Late visionary artist Aminah Brenda Lynn Robinson celebrated in second solo show at Fort Gansevoort
summary: Fort Gansevoort is presenting its second solo exhibition devoted to late visionary Ohio artist Aminah Brenda Lynn Robinson (1940–2015). Beaded and Bound brings together twenty-five handmade books, mixed-media textile works, and intricately embellished dolls to celebrate Robinson’s devotion to storytelling through unconventional materials and formats. Combining embroidery, appliqué, drawing, painting, collage, assemblage, and vernacular writing, the artist wove personal memories, family histories, and local narratives into richly tactile, sometimes peculiar, and always moving works alive with the histories of the African diaspora. Aminah Robinson was a prolific writer and natural storyteller who regarded bookmaking as a vital vehicle for formal and narrative experimentation. Beginning in the 1980s, she constructed elaborate handmade volumes, sometimes working on individual books over the course of several decades. title: New Britain Museum of American Art highlights Mary Cassatt's role in bringing Impressionism to America
summary: The New Britain Museum of American Art is presenting the exhibition Among Friends: Mary Cassatt and Her Circle, on view November 7, 2026 – February 14, 2027. The artist Mary Cassatt (1844–1926) was the only American to exhibit with the French Impressionists, a radical group of artists in Paris who rejected the conventions of the Academic Salon. She remarked that when the artist Edgar Degas invited her to join the group, "At last, I could work with absolute independence." Cassatt prized her artistic freedom and is renowned today for her pioneering vision. Her treatment of everyday domestic life as a legitimate subject for art, determination to work as a professional woman artist, and daring experimentations across media were groundbreaking for their time. title: Art on the Underground unveils Hurvin Anderson's 'Universal Travel' at Brixton station
summary: ‘Universal Travel’ is a new artwork for Brixton Underground station by British painter Hurvin Anderson. Launched on 19 November 2026, Anderson’s site-specific artwork will be on view for a year. It draws upon a close connection to Brixton, where the artist has lived for extended periods, holding a studio in Tulse Hill since 1998. ‘Universal Travel’ marks the 10th commission for Brixton Underground station in a series that has responded to the diverse narratives of local murals painted in the 1980s and rapid development of the area, highlighting its history as a home for Black communities since the arrival of HMT Empire Windrush at Tilbury Docks in 1948. Anderson’s paintings frequently reflect on diasporic life in the UK, and the postcolonial Caribbean landscape, drawing upon his upbringing in Birmingham by Jamaican parents, and time spent in Trinidad. title: Forum Gallery presents recent pastel still-lifes by G. Daniel Massad spanning 2014 to 2026
summary: Forum Gallery presents recent pastel works by G. Daniel Massad (b. 1946). Recognized for his meticulously rendered, extraordinarily detailed and poetic still-lifes, Massad’s works are rife with theatrical drama, revealing their stories through carefully orchestrated objects and symbols. Massad completes at most three works in any given year. His compositional ideas take two to three years for gestation, starting with a first foggy vision of its essence, with each element considered and worked through mentally beforehand. The eleven works on view in our presentation date from 2014 to 2026. Four are a part of a group of works recently completed by the Artist on a small, intimate scale. Mr. Massad describes his shift to focus on “little jewels” as occurring in 2022, when he began a series to describe natural objects as a botanist might approach them, investigating them closely with scientific precision. title: Corning Museum of Glass appoints Dr. Jennifer Cohen as Director of Collections and Curatorial Affairs
summary: Corning Museum of Glass announced the appointment of Dr. Jennifer Cohen as its new Director of Collections and Curatorial Affairs. Cohen will join the Museum in January 2027, providing vision for CMoG’s collection of more than 50,000 objects spanning 3,500 years of global human history, its internationally renowned exhibition program, and its sector-leading glass conservation and scholarship. Cohen joins CMoG from The Dalí Museum in St. Petersburg, Florida, where she served as Director of Curatorial Affairs since 2023. In that role, she has directed institutional collection strategy, cultivated a portfolio of international museum partnerships from the Museum of Fine Arts Boston to the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid, and developed ambitious multi-year exhibition programs that encompassed the historical legacy of Salvador Dalí and current contemporary practice. title: Third edition of paper positions vienna closes with strong sales and high attendance
summary: On Sunday evening, the third edition of paper positions vienna came to a successful close. Twenty-eight galleries travelled to Vienna from Austria, Germany, Italy, Slovenia and Latvia to present outstanding works of art on and made from paper, running alongside Vienna Art Week. A large crowd made their way to the impressive Semper Depot, which now serves as the studio complex for the Academy of Fine Arts. Visitors showed great interest in the exhibits at the specialised fair and, with a discerning eye, praised the high quality of the works and the presentations. The atmosphere was excellent, not only amongst the visitors but also amongst the exhibitors. The local galleries agreed that this fair format is a perfect fit for Vienna: they intend to continue actively supporting the development of paper positions in the future. In short: everything was wonderful.

title: Museion presents 2027 exhibition program
summary: Museion presents its 2027 program. The exhibitions form part of “THE SOFTEST HARD”, Museion’s research line exploring art as a social and urban practice and a nonviolent form of resistance. At a time when social cohesion and democratic culture can no longer be taken for granted, it asks what a quiet radicality can achieve: how art can hold complexity, create spaces for dialogue, and undermine entrenched divisions. In spring 2027, Museion will present the first solo museum exhibition in Italy of Zoe Leonard (b. 1961 in Liberty, NY, US). Developed in close collaboration with the New York–based artist, it will bring together recent photographs and sculptures across the museum’s two largest floors. title: Kunsthaus Zürich presents Ralph Lemon and Kevin Beasley sound and performance exhibition
summary: From 20 November 2026 to 3 January 2027, Ralph Lemon and Kevin Beasley's exhibition "Residuum (Tell it anyway)" turns the Müller building at the Kunsthaus Zürich into a resonant space for sound and performance. It investigates what remains after a live moment has passed, and how history and memory are written into bodies, voices and sounds. "Residuum (Tell it anyway)" invites visitors to listen and rediscover the architecture of part of the Kunsthaus: the Müller building, an extension named after its architect, Erwin Müller (1925–2017). When it was inaugurated in 1976, the building's openness was considered a radical architectural gesture. As a result, light, movable walls were introduced so that individual presentations could be shaped – much like the flexible layout of a trade fair pavilion. title: Kunstraum Dornbirn opens an exhibition featuring Ursula Palla's bronze sculptures of wild flora
summary: Maverick vegetation takes possession of Kunstraum Dornbirn. Dark stalks, leaves, and blossoms, some scarcely knee-high, others looming larger than life, sprout within the remains of the former industrial architecture. Rootstocks stand upon the concrete floor as if violently torn from the earth; elsewhere, stalks appear to emerge directly from the ground itself. What at first appears to be a barren landscape, threatened by decay, proves upon closer inspection to be permanent and weighty: the plants are cast in bronze, each one unique. Every detail, leaf vein, and thorn is visible. It is not to splendid blooms or botanical rarities that Palla raises this sculptural monument. title: Silverlens announces representation of Jen Liu
summary: Silverlens announced its co-representation of Jen Liu. The news follows Pound of Flesh, her 2026 exhibition at Silverlens New York. MoMA acquired two paintings from the show, part of her interdisciplinary series New Humans. A Taiwanese-American artist born and based in New York, Liu works across video, painting, biomaterial, programming, and performance. Her palette is fleshy pink, molten silver-gold, powder-coated white, and satin black; her imagery pulls together stilettos, breathing cubes of meat, animatronic eyes, and gold pearls. The polish is a luxury ad’s, the logic a cartoon’s, all set to an ambient hum of body horror. Liu researches histories of labor and diasporic Asian identity, and how they are entangled with the global politics of technology. title: Philip Larratt-Smith curates YAGEO Foundation collection exhibition
summary: The Scorpion and the Frog derives its title from a Russian fable in which a scorpion asks a frog to carry him across a river. At first the frog refuses for fear of being stung, but is persuaded when the scorpion says this would be illogical as then he too would drown. When they are halfway across, the frog feels a terrible pain and knows that he has been stung. As they slip below the water, the frog asks, ‘Where is the logic in this?’ to which the scorpion replies, “None, but I cannot help it. It’s my character.” The exhibition presents a selection of masterpieces from the YAGEO Foundation through the framing concept of the mind-body divide, an opposition that runs like a fault line through the collection. title: Staley-Wise Gallery presents a retrospective of pioneering photographer Genevieve Naylor
summary: Genevieve Naylor was a photographer whose remarkable career was diverse and encompassed photojournalism, portrait, and fashion photography. From her early days as one of the first women hired at the Associated Press to a government sponsored assignment to Brazil, she then photographed fashion for Harper's Bazaar while also documenting Eleanor Roosevelt for nearly 4 years. Naylor touched all the bases in photography in the golden age of magazines and was a woman of great talent and sophistication, which is apparent in her work as seen in this exhibition. Born into a distinguished Republican family in Springfield, Massachusetts in 1915, Naylor attended a private boarding school. title: The Ringling unveils major exhibition celebrating recent photography acquisitions
summary: The John and Mable Ringling Museum of Art announced the exhibition, Acquisitions in Photography: 2020–2025, on view through May 9, 2027, in the Museum of Art’s Ulla R. and Arthur F. Searing Wing (Galleries A + B). The exhibition showcases a curated selection of highlights from more than 1,200 photographic works acquired by the museum since 2020 through generous donor gifts and institutional purchases. “From its analog and chemical roots to its ubiquitous digital presence today, photography has transformed how we understand the world and communicate our experiences,” says Christopher Jones, Stanton B. and Nancy W. title: Bienvenu Steinberg & C presents Martí Cormands tenth solo exhibition in New York
summary: Bienvenu Steinberg & C is presenting Mirroring, an exhibition of new paintings by Spanish-born artist Martí Cormand, his tenth in New York. The exhibition will be on view from November 19 to December 19, 2026. In Mirroring, Martí Cormand addresses the dichotomy between the original and the copy. Working with museum catalogues of European paintings—mostly from the medieval and Baroque periods—he focuses on the diffuse reflection of the images projected on the gloss of the adjacent page. The result is a game of doubles and mirages. From the time humans understood their reflection on the surface of water to be a visual fiction to our own era’s obsession with selfies, the mirror image has transitioned from being a natural phenomenon to a fundamental artifact.
